title: Reading Charts
tagline: Candles, trends, support and resistance, and breakouts you can trust.

levels.title: Candlestick Anatomy
levels.summary: One candle holds four prices. Learn to read who won the day.
objectives: Read open, high, low and close from a candle.

terms.definition: Open, high, low and close: the four prices a candle shows for one period.
The thick part of a candle, from the open to the close.
The thin line above or below the body, reaching the high or the low. Also called a shadow.
A candle that closed above its open, usually shown in green.
A candle that closed below its open, usually shown in red.

cards.title: Line versus candle
cards.body: A **line chart** joins each day's closing price. A **candlestick** shows four prices for each day: **open, high, low and close (OHLC)**. Candles tell you not just where the price ended, but how it got there.

cards.title: Body and wicks
cards.body: The **body** runs from the open to the close. The thin **wicks** (or shadows) reach up to the high and down to the low. A candle with Open $20.00, High $21.50, Low $19.80, Close $21.20 has a body from $20.00 to $21.20. Drag the handles to build one.

cards.title: Green and red
cards.body: A **green** (bullish) candle closed above its open. A **red** (bearish) candle closed below its open. You can change the colours in settings, and every candle also carries a text label, so colour is never the only clue.

cards.title: What a candle says
cards.body: A long green body means buyers controlled the day. A long red body means sellers did. A long upper wick means buyers pushed the price up but sellers pushed it back down before the close. Closing near the low is a sign of selling pressure.

check.prompt: What does a long green candlestick usually indicate?

options.text: Buyers in control, pushing the price up

check.explanation: It closed well above its open.

check.prompt: A candle has Open 20.00, High 21.50, Low 19.80, Close 21.20. What colour is it?
check.explanation: The close is above the open, so it is green (bullish).

check.prompt: A candle has Open 35.00, High 35.40, Low 31.90, Close 32.10. Which is true?

options.text: It closed near its low, so sellers were in control
It has a long lower wick

check.explanation: It closed just $0.20 above the low after opening near the high.

check.prompt: The wick above the body shows the period's highest traded price.
check.explanation: The top of the upper wick is the high.

levels.title: Candlestick Patterns
levels.summary: Doji, hammer, shooting star and engulfing: useful clues, never promises.
objectives: Recognize the doji, hammer, shooting star and engulfing patterns.
Explain that patterns are probabilities that need context and confirmation.

terms.definition: A candle whose open and close are almost equal, showing indecision.
A small body near the top with a long lower wick, after a decline. A possible bullish reversal.
A small body near the bottom with a long upper wick, after a rise. A possible bearish reversal.
A candle whose body completely covers the previous candle's body in the opposite colour.
Evidence from the next candle or candles that a pattern's signal is playing out.

cards.title: Doji: indecision
cards.body: In a **doji**, the open and close are almost the same, leaving a tiny body. Buyers and sellers ended the day balanced. Open $30.00, close $30.02, with wicks on both sides, is a doji.

cards.title: Hammer and shooting star
cards.body: A **hammer** has a small body near the top and a lower wick at least twice the body, after a decline: sellers pushed down, buyers fought back. A **shooting star** is the mirror image at the top of a rise, a possible bearish reversal.

cards.title: Engulfing
cards.body: A **bullish engulfing** pattern is a green body that completely covers the previous red body, after a downtrend. Day 1: open $52, close $50. Day 2: open $49.80, close $52.60. A **bearish engulfing** pattern is the opposite, after an uptrend.

cards.title: Clues, not promises
cards.body: Patterns fail often. Check **where** the pattern appears (after a trend, at support), check the volume, and wait for **confirmation**: a next candle that closes in the expected direction. If you act on it, plan a stop beyond the pattern's low or high.

check.prompt: After 5 red days, a candle prints Open 39.70, High 40.10, Low 38.00, Close 40.00. Which pattern is it?
check.explanation: The lower wick ($1.70) is far longer than the body ($0.30), which sits near the top.

check.prompt: Day 1: Open 52, Close 50 (red). Day 2: Open 49.80, Close 52.60 (green). Which pattern is it?
check.explanation: Day 2's green body covers all of Day 1's red body.

check.prompt: A candle prints Open 30.00, High 30.90, Low 29.20, Close 30.02. Which pattern is it?
check.explanation: The open and close are almost equal, with wicks on both sides.

check.prompt: You spot a hammer after a long downtrend. What is the most reasonable action?

options.text: Buy the maximum; the reversal is guaranteed
Treat it as a possible reversal: wait for confirmation and plan a stop below the hammer's low

check.explanation: A pattern is a clue; confirmation and a stop handle the times it fails.

levels.title: Trends & Trendlines
levels.summary: Higher highs and higher lows. Trade with the trend until it breaks.
objectives: Identify uptrends, downtrends and ranges from swing highs and lows.
Recognize signs that a trend is breaking.

terms.definition: A series of higher highs and higher lows.
A series of lower highs and lower lows.
A sideways market that moves between a floor and a ceiling without trending.
A peak or dip where the price turned.
A line joining two or more rising lows (uptrend) or falling highs (downtrend).

cards.title: Higher highs, higher lows
cards.body: An **uptrend** has rising peaks and rising dips: highs of $50, $54, $58 and lows of $46, $49, $53. A **downtrend** has lower highs and lower lows. A **range** (a sideways market) has neither.

cards.title: Trade with the trend
cards.body: Trends often persist for a while, so many traders only buy in the trend's direction and hold while it lasts. In a game where you can only buy and sell, that means buying uptrends and standing aside in downtrends.

cards.title: Trendlines
cards.body: To draw an uptrend line, connect two or more rising **lows**. For a downtrend, connect two or more falling **highs**. The line shows where the trend has been finding support. Tap two lows on the chart to draw one.

cards.title: When a trend breaks
cards.body: A close below the uptrend line, followed by a bounce that fails below the previous high, is a warning: the pattern of higher highs has stopped. One break is not proof, but it is a good moment to tighten your stop or step aside.

check.prompt: Swing highs are $50, $54, $58; swing lows are $46, $49, $53. What is the trend?
check.explanation: Both the highs and the lows are rising.

check.prompt: Swing highs are $80, $76, $71; swing lows are $74, $69, $65. What is the trend?
check.explanation: Lower highs and lower lows make a downtrend.

check.prompt: How do you draw an uptrend line?

options.text: Draw a horizontal line at the average price
Join the first close to the last close

check.explanation: An uptrend line runs under the rising swing lows.

check.prompt: In an uptrend, the price closes below the trendline and the next bounce fails below the previous high. What does this suggest?

options.text: The trend may be weakening or reversing

check.explanation: A trendline break plus a lower high is a warning, not proof.

levels.title: Support & Resistance
levels.summary: Floors where buyers step in, ceilings where sellers appear, and how they swap roles.
objectives: Find support and resistance from repeated turning points.
Place entries, stops and targets around levels.

terms.definition: A price zone where falls have repeatedly stopped because buyers stepped in.
A price zone where rises have repeatedly stalled because sellers appeared.
When broken resistance later acts as support, or broken support as resistance.
A return to a broken level to check whether it now holds from the other side.

cards.title: Floors and ceilings
cards.body: **Support** is a level where falls have repeatedly stopped because buyers step in. **Resistance** is where rises have stalled because sellers appear. Orchard Foods bouncing near $48 three times and topping near $52 twice gives a floor at $48 and a ceiling at $52.

cards.title: Why levels matter (sometimes)
cards.body: Many traders watch the same levels, so orders cluster there, and round numbers like $50 often matter. Treat levels as **zones**, not exact lines: a floor at $48 might hold anywhere from $47.70 to $48.30. Levels break too.

cards.title: Role reversal
cards.body: When resistance breaks, it often acts as support on a later retest: the old ceiling becomes the new floor. Lumen Bikes breaks above $52, pulls back to $52 a week later and bounces. Broken support can likewise become resistance.

cards.title: Using levels
cards.body: Buy near support with a stop just below the zone, and aim for a target near resistance. Buying Orchard Foods at $48.30 with a stop at $47.20 and a target at $51.80 risks $1.10 to make $3.50. Drag the stop and target to compare reward with risk.

check.prompt: A chart bounces near $48 on days 3, 9 and 15 and tops out near $55 on days 6 and 12. What are support and resistance?
check.explanation: Falls stop near $48 (support); rises stall near $55 (resistance).

check.prompt: The price breaks above $55 on high volume, later pulls back to $55 and holds. What is $55 acting as now?
check.explanation: Role reversal: the old ceiling became a floor.

check.prompt: You are buying near the $48 support zone at $48.30. Where is a sensible stop?

options.text: Just below the support zone, about $46.90

check.explanation: Below the zone, so normal wiggles don't hit it, but not so far that the loss is huge.

check.prompt: Support levels are exact prices that can never be broken.
check.explanation: Levels are zones, and they do break.

levels.title: Volume & Breakouts
levels.summary: Tell a real breakout from a fake one, and plan the trade before it happens.
objectives: Use volume to judge how strong a move is.
Tell a confirmed breakout from a false one.
Plan a breakout trade with an entry, a stop-loss and a measured-move target.

terms.definition: A close beyond resistance (or below support) after a range.
A move beyond a level that quickly falls back into the range. Also called a bull trap.
A rough breakout target: the breakout level plus the height of the range.
The typical number of shares traded per day, used to judge whether today is unusual.

cards.title: Volume confirms
cards.body: A rise on growing volume shows many traders are joining in. A rise on shrinking volume is weaker: fewer participants, easier to reverse. Look at the volume bars under the price before trusting a big candle.

cards.title: Breakouts
cards.body: A **breakout** happens when the price closes beyond resistance (or below support) after a range. It is more convincing on volume well above average, about 1.5–2 times normal, and often follows real news such as strong earnings.

cards.title: False breakouts
cards.body: In a **false breakout**, or bull trap, the price pokes above resistance on weak volume or an unconfirmed rumour, then falls back into the range. Defences: wait for a **close** above the level, check the volume, and keep your stop back inside the range.

cards.title: The breakout plan
cards.body: Enter after a confirmed close above resistance, put the stop-loss back inside the range, and set a rough target of breakout level + range height (the **measured move**). Range $40–$44: target $48. Real brokers also let you pre-place a buy stop just above resistance.

check.prompt: Which is the most convincing breakout?

options.text: It pokes above resistance during the day but closes below, on low volume
It closes above resistance on twice the average volume
It closes above resistance on half the average volume

check.explanation: A close beyond the level with strong volume is the best evidence.

check.prompt: A stock ranged between $40 and $44 for 15 days. On day 16: High 44.80, Close 43.60, volume 0.7× average. What happened?
check.explanation: It poked above $44 but closed back inside the range on low volume.

check.prompt: Range $40–$44, breakout at $44. What is the measured-move target?
check.explanation: The range height is $4, so $44 + $4 = $48.

check.prompt: You bought the breakout at $44.20. Where is a logical stop?
check.explanation: If the price falls back into the range, the breakout has failed.
